summary: Del Norte County site listed under Siskiyou NF; the only dated source is a 1940 guard-placement note on lightning and roads. No build date or present state found.

events.note: A May 1940 guard-placement entry describes what the position could see and says road improvements would raise its value for fire suppression.

evidence.supports: Listing places High Divide in Del Norte County under Siskiyou National Forest
evidence.quote: Del Norte County - Siskiyou National Forest

evidence.supports: May 1940 entry: view covered a lightning area; man-caused fires several miles to the south
evidence.quote: Seen area covers lightning area. Some man-caused fires several miles to the south.

evidence.supports: Position would have higher value for suppression once roads are improved
evidence.quote: When the roads are improved this position will have higher value for suppression than it has now.

evidence.supports: Directory lists Low Divide (Stone Corral) in Del Norte County
Directory marks the Low Divide (Stone Corral) tower as gone

notes_for_editor: Only two sources, and the one dated record is a single 1940 plan entry. No construction date, staffing after 1940, fate or present state appears in any source found. Two web searches and several page reads turned up nothing on a High Divide lookout history. The brief's coordinates (41.9069, -124.0559) are roughly 4 km from the directory's Low Divide (Stone Corral) entry (41.92771, -124.01854, tower gone); my calculation, unverified whether they are the same site, and the story does not link them. Possible next steps: Six Rivers NF or Del Norte County Historical Society records, and a check of whether High Divide and Low Divide are one site. The 1940 record is cited as 'Siskiyou National Forest' and the current managing forest is not verified.
